QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_39

question.text: Which element of a Theory of Change is MOST important for the SIA to test during evidence collection because it is typically the point where programs fail silently?

answer.text: Assumptions — the preconditions presumed necessary for the causal pathway to hold

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Assumptions are the 'silent hinges' of a ToC. Inputs/activities/outputs are usually easy to measure; it is the untested assumptions (parents will allow girls to attend, market will hire trained youth, donors will continue funding) whose failure kills programs. The SIA must identify and test each material assumption. **The Trap:** Inputs and activities are inputs-side, easily observed. Impact is the end-point claim whose plausibility DEPENDS on assumptions holding. That is why assumptions deserve scrutiny. **Cross-Exam Context:** XXIII Ch 5 ToC and Ch 6 both flag assumption-testing as the core SIA discipline. X-A IA uses 'key assumption risks' in investment thesis. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Maintain a 'Top 5 Assumption Risks' register in every engagement — for each, note the evidence sought and the actual evidence found. Any red flag gets disclosed in the SIR's limitations section.
